retry_contract.invalid_rerank: Fall back to validated fused order without another executor repair
retry_contract.provider_attempt_definition: One initial attempt plus at most two retries equals at most three total attempts. GT099 asserts the observed attempt count is <= 3.

POST /sessions.request: No caller-supplied authorization overrides; server derives authenticated scope and seeds the traveler profile including grade
POST /sessions.response: session_id, organization_id and an opaque bearer token derived by the server

POST /receipts.request: multipart session_id and files[]; max five JPEG/PNG, 10 MiB each

POST /travel/search.response: offers[], recommended_ids[], provisional_ids[], noncompliant_ids[], evidence[], limitations[]

api_contract.common: 401/403 unauthorized access, 400/422 invalid structured request, 413 size/count limit, 415 unsupported image. Domain clarification is a normal response. Tool/provider errors are bounded and disclosed. No booking routes.

GET /health.request: Unauthenticated liveness probe; performs no database, index, model or provider call
GET /health.response: 200 {status, app_version, commit}. Used by the Compose healthcheck and the ALB target group

GET /ready.response: 200 when the policy index version, rule registry, checkpoint store and model configuration all resolve; 503 with the failing component otherwise. Never returns secrets

DELETE /sessions/{session_id}.response: 204 after deleting session state, checkpoints, cached offers and every upload owned by the session

DELETE /receipts/{image_id}.response: 204 after deleting the stored image and its extraction; assessments that depended on it are invalidated and recomputed as incomplete

error_envelope.rule: Domain clarification is a normal 200 response carrying missing_fields, not an error. Error bodies never contain credentials, file system paths or another session record.

api_contract.openapi: api/openapi.json is generated from FastAPI in M2 and committed as a derived artifact.

POST /admin/policies.request: Administrator only. Multipart form: title, version, authority policy|guidance, geography, effective_from, effective_to, and exactly one of file (.txt/.md, at most 2 MiB) or text
POST /admin/policies.response: 201 document metadata and section count; 403 FORBIDDEN_ROLE for other roles; 413/415/422 for limits

GET /policy/library.response: core policy sections and added library documents

entrypoint_contract_rules: These names are the only interface the evaluation driver may call. maps_to is the planned application function; rename it only by updating this contract in the same change.
input_fields and result_fields are the union observed across the mapped golden cases. A driver must accept every listed input field and must populate every result field the case asserts.
A component entrypoint tests one operation and must not fail because unrelated claim fields are absent. A workflow entrypoint runs normal application behavior with injected clock and fixtures.

observation_fields are JSON-pointer suffixes under /observations/ taken from the cases' automatic checks. They are produced by harness instrumentation, never by the model or the application response body.
No entrypoint may branch on a GT identifier, read tests/, or receive expected values.
authority_order: policy_sources/policy.json and policy_sources/rule_registry.json — fictional business rules and every number used in arithmetic
policy_sources/reference_data.json — enumerations, aliases, FX fixtures and controlled vocabularies
IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT.json, docs/REQUIREMENTS.json, docs/TEST_PROTOCOL.txt, schemas/ — interface and evaluation detail
Everything else is derived or explanatory and never overrides the above

derived_artifacts.rule: Derived files are generated by build_package.py and are never hand-edited. validate_package.py fails when a derived file drifts from its source.

identity.principle: Organization, session scope and traveler grade are server-held. Neither the user message nor any model output can override them.
identity.prototype_scheme: POST /sessions returns an opaque session token bound server-side to organization_id, session_id and traveler profile. Every other route requires Authorization: Bearer <token>. Unknown, expired or foreign tokens return 401/403 before any model, retrieval or provider call.
identity.ui_to_api: Streamlit holds the token server-side in its session state and forwards it on each FastAPI call. The token is never rendered into the browser page, a URL or a log line.
identity.grade_authority: grade comes from the server-held traveler profile seeded when the session is created. A grade stated in chat is an unverified hint: it may trigger a clarification but never selects a higher cap. Golden cases supply grade as seeded profile context, not as a user assertion.
identity.deployment_scheme: In AWS the ALB/Cognito identity is verified (signer, expiry, audience) at the reverse proxy and exchanged for the same server-side session. An internal container URL never establishes identity. See docs/AWS_DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.txt DEP02.
identity.test_construction: A golden case starts with a fresh authorized session created through the same code path; GT113 proves a second session B record stays unreachable from session A.
identity.role_authority: role (employee or admin) comes from config/profiles.toml with the session, like grade. Only admin may manage the policy library. The client cannot supply a role.

router.rule: Routing is a deterministic function of the validated request, never a model choice, so that simple-path and full-agent latency can be compared.
decision_order: Any attached image or pending receipt confirmation -> receipt_review
A travel search intent with a search_type, route or destination plus dates -> travel_search
A correction or follow-up that invalidates stored results -> the route that produced them
Retrieval returns equally authoritative conflicting rules for the asked applicability -> escalate the current route to the planner/critic path
router.escalation_note: policy_simple runs clarify -> retrieve -> generate -> validate citations with no planner and no critic model call. Escalation is recorded in the trace as route_escalated with its trigger.

retention.enforcement: A scheduled cleanup task inside the API process deletes expired uploads and traces and records the count it removed. Expiry is evaluated against the injected clock so it is testable.
retention.user_deletion: DELETE /sessions/{session_id} and DELETE /receipts/{image_id} delete on request ahead of the schedule.
retention.deployment_note: In AWS, deletion must also clear S3 noncurrent versions and account for backup retention; a lifecycle rule alone does not give an exact deletion time (DEP05).
retention.verification: Covered by implementation tests AC19 in docs/REQUIREMENTS.json and docs/TEST_PROTOCOL.txt section 8, not by the frozen 120-case suite.

money_representation.application_output: Finite decimal string with exactly two fractional digits, for example "22260.00". Unknown amounts are null, never 0 and never omitted.
money_representation.golden_fixtures: Existing expected values are JSON numbers such as 22260.0 and 1.7. The evaluator compares with Decimal(str(value)), so "22260.00" equals 22260.0. Do not rewrite the fixtures and do not serialize floats.
money_representation.rounding: ROUND_HALF_UP per converted line at two digits; the signed residual is reported as rounding_adjustment_inr and is never a policy violation.

prompting_strategies.a_basic: Instruction plus retrieved evidence, free-form answer.
prompting_strategies.b_structured: Instruction plus evidence plus a required JSON answer schema with explicit evidence_ids, missing_fields and limitations.
prompting_strategies.c_few_shot: The structured prompt plus two or three worked examples drawn only from development-split cases.
prompting_strategies.rule: All three run against the same fixed evidence, the same small model and the same held-out protocol. Prompt files live in prompts/ with a recorded prompt hash. Held-out cases are never used as examples.
